import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** give your app a web page that the cluster itself serves from the
signed release, that signs people in with their passkey, and that calls the
app as them, without ever getting more of their account than the app needs.

The cluster serves a release's frontend from the `.mpk` it verified, on an
origin of the package's own, so the page is exactly what the publisher signed.
A passkey ceremony from that origin opens a session **bound to the package**:
it reaches only instances of that package. What it may not do (approve an
upgrade, create an organization, invite someone), the page asks the node's
consent page for.
The protocol is in [Packages & frontends](/protocol/applications/#frontends),
[Package-bound sessions](/protocol/identities/#package-bound-sessions) and
[The consent page](/protocol/consent-page/).

## Build the page for the cluster

The node serves each file with a fixed content security policy:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; img-src 'self' data: blob:;
font-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none';
form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'; connect-src 'self' <the cluster's API origins> <the attestation mirror>
```

So the build must:

- **ship everything it loads.** No script, style, font or image from another
  origin; the page reaches only the cluster's API (and the attestation mirror
  mero-js reads release measurements and Intel's collateral from).
- **run no inline script.** Inline styles are allowed, inline `<script>` and
  `on*=` handlers are not.
- **use relative URLs.** The page is served under `/{version}/`, so an
  absolute `/assets/app.js` misses; build with a relative base (Vite
  `base: './'`) and no `<base>` element.
- **use only these file types:** `html`, `js`, `mjs`, `css`, `json`,
  `webmanifest`, `txt`, `svg`, `png`, `jpg`, `jpeg`, `gif`, `webp`, `ico`,
  `woff`, `woff2`, `ttf`, `wasm`, `webm`, `xml`.
- **stay under 32 MiB** for all files together (`MAX_FRONTEND_BYTES`).

`calimero_bundle::check_frontend_html` is the lint a bundling tool can run on
the build output for the first three rules (`FRONTEND_REMOTE_RESOURCE`,
`FRONTEND_INLINE_SCRIPT`, `FRONTEND_ESCAPING_URL`); the node does not run it
and relies on the policy above.

## Put it in the release

The manifest names the files under `frontend`, each with its SHA-256 and size,
so the publisher's signature covers them; the archive carries them under
`frontend/`:

```json
{
  "package": "com.example.notes",
  "appVersion": "1.0.0",
  "wasm": { "path": "app.wasm", "hash": "…", "size": 48213 },
  "frontend": {
    "entry": "frontend/index.html",
    "files": [
      { "path": "frontend/index.html", "hash": "…", "size": 412 },
      { "path": "frontend/assets/app.js", "hash": "…", "size": 90321 }
    ]
  }
}
```

`scripts/pack-component.py --frontend <dir>` writes it: every file under the
build directory goes into the archive as `frontend/<path>` with its SHA-256 and
size, and `--frontend-entry` (default `index.html`) names the page served at
`/`. The script refuses, before signing, what the node would refuse at install
(the rules below), so a bad build fails on your machine, not on the cluster.

```bash
npm run build                                    # writes dist/ with base './'
mero-app-build apps/notes --out app.wasm
python3 -I scripts/pack-component.py --wasm app.wasm --frontend dist \
  --package com.example.notes --app-version 1.0.0 --key my-signing-key.json \
  --out dist-mpk/com.example.notes-1.0.0.mpk
meroctl app install --path dist-mpk/com.example.notes-1.0.0.mpk   # a development cluster
```

At install the node refuses a frontend whose paths are not canonical paths
under `frontend/` (`FRONTEND_UNSAFE_PATH`), listed twice
(`FRONTEND_DUPLICATE_PATH`), of a type it does not serve
(`FRONTEND_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`), over 32 MiB (`FRONTEND_TOO_LARGE`), whose
entry is missing or not HTML (`FRONTEND_NO_ENTRY`, `FRONTEND_ENTRY_NOT_HTML`),
or whose bytes do not match the manifest (`FRONTEND_SIZE_MISMATCH`,
`FRONTEND_HASH_MISMATCH`, `FRONTEND_MISSING_FILE`).

A release that changes only the frontend is a release like any other: an
instance moves to it with an upgrade ([Ship a new version](/build/ship-v2/)).

## Where it is served

Only on a cluster started with `--apps-domain D` (`merod local` uses
`localhost`). Each package gets a host of its own, `{label}.D`, where the label
is 52 base32 characters of the package's hashed name
(`calimero_node::app_host::label`).

| Path | Serves |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | redirects to `/{newest version}/` |
| `/{version}/{path}` | that release's file; any other path under the version is the entry, for client-side routes |
| `/app/{app}/{path}` | redirects to `/{version}/{path}` of the release that instance runs, so a link you give a customer keeps opening the frontend that matches their instance |
| `/d/{deployment}/{path}` | redirects to `/{version}/{path}?deployment={id}`, the release that deployment offers |
| `/.well-known/calimero.json` | `{ package, versions, deployments, api }`: the releases, the deployments offering the package and the cluster's API URLs |

Every redirect keeps the query, so `/?invite=…` reaches the page with its token.
Only `GET` and `HEAD` are served; an unknown label is a `404`, never a node
route.
The same site is also on the package's cluster host (for Calimero Cloud's
resolver), on each deployment's own host, and on any custom domain you
register ([below](#serve-it-on-your-own-domain)).

## Sign people in from the page

<SeqDiagram id="d-guide-frontend" title="A served frontend signs someone in and calls its app"
  lanes={[
    { label: 'Browser', color: '#f0883e' },
    { label: '{label}.D', color: '#a371f7' },
    { label: 'Node API (sealed)', color: '#3fb950' },
    { label: 'Passkey', color: '#58a6ff' },
  ]}
  steps={[
    { from: 0, to: 1, label: 'GET /app/{app}/ → /1.0.0/' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, label: 'signed files, CSP', dashed: true },
    { from: 0, to: 1, label: 'GET /.well-known/calimero.json' },
    { from: 0, to: 2, label: 'attest the node, open the sealed channel' },
    { from: 0, to: 2, label: 'sign in, origin = the page' },
    { from: 0, to: 3, label: 'navigator.credentials.get' },
    { from: 3, to: 0, label: 'assertion', dashed: true },
    { from: 2, to: 0, label: 'session bound to com.example.notes', dashed: true },
    { from: 0, to: 2, label: 'call notes app' },
  ]} />

```ts
import {
  CalimeroClient, browserPasskey, frontendManifest, pageDeployment, PasskeyUnknownHere,
} from '@calimero-network/mero-js';

const { package: pkg, api } = await frontendManifest();     // this page's /.well-known/calimero.json
const client = new CalimeroClient({
  baseUrl: api[0],
  nodes: api.slice(1),
  policy: { release: { minReleaseVersion: '2.3.109' } },  // { allowMock: true } on merod local
});

const saved = sessionStorage.getItem('calimero');
if (saved) client.useSession(JSON.parse(saved));
else {
  try {
    sessionStorage.setItem('calimero', JSON.stringify(await client.signIn(browserPasskey())));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof PasskeyUnknownHere) showSignUp(); // client.signUp(browserPasskey(), name)
    else throw e;
  }
}

// Opened through /d/{deployment}/: create the person's instance from that deployment.
const deployment = pageDeployment();
const { appId } = deployment
  ? await client.apps.create({ name: 'My notes', deployment, package: pkg })
  : { appId: appFromPath() };
await client.apps.call({ app: appId, method: 'add', args: { text: 'hello' } });
```

- The well-known file is fetched in the clear and only says where the API is;
  trust comes from the attestation the client checks before it sends
  anything.
- In a browser, `signIn` and `signUp` send the page's origin when it is not
  one of the client's nodes, and the node answers with the relying-party id
  to use. The session is bound to the package of that origin; `me()` answers
  its `app` and `origin`.
- A passkey made on another cluster, or removed, is `401 PASSKEY_UNKNOWN_HERE`
  (`PasskeyUnknownHere`).
- Keep the session in `sessionStorage` and `useSession` it after a reload, so
  the person is not prompted again.

## What a frontend session may do

It acts as the person, but only within its package:

| May | May not |
| --- | --- |
| call and read instances of its package, and list them | reach any other app of the account |
| create instances of its package (from a deployment, or by package) | manage passkeys, API keys, recovery or sessions |
| upload blobs and files to its apps, follow their events and presence | approve releases, outbound hosts or upgrades; install or uninstall packages |
| step up with a passkey for one of its apps' `confirm` methods, from its own origin | create, rename or delete organizations, invite, redeem invites, change members |
| manage the teams **below** its package's app team (create, rename, move within, members, delete when all their apps are its package's), for apps such as a chat's channels | change the app team itself, an app's access outside those teams, or delete an app |

Everything in the right column is refused (`403`) whatever the person's own
rights. The person still has those rights; the page sends them to the node's
consent page to use one.

## Ask for consent

For an upgrade, a release approval, outbound hosts, or an organization change,
the page asks the node for a consent request and sends the person to the
node's own page, where they see what they approve (from the node's state and
the signed manifests, not from your page) and confirm with their passkey.

```ts
import { createOrgConsent, upgradeConsent } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';

const returnTo = `${location.origin}${location.pathname}`;
await client.openConsentPage(upgradeConsent(appId, '1.1.0', returnTo), {
  confirm: async ({ code }) => code === undefined || window.confirm(`The next page shows ${code}. Continue?`),
});

// Back on returnTo?request_id=…&result=…: read the decision from the node, never the URL.
const decision = await client.resumeConsent();
if (decision?.status === 'approved' && decision.kind === 'createOrg') useOrg(decision.outcome);
```

`openConsentPage` posts `POST /consent/requests { kind, scope?, subject,
returnTo }` (any session of the account, a bound one included) and navigates
to the answer's `url`. The kinds are `release`, `upgrade`, `outbound`,
`createOrg`, `createInvite`, `acceptInvite`, `leaveOrg`, `removeMember`,
`setMemberRole`, `setMemberTeams`, `removeMemberTeams`, `revokeInvite`,
`renameOrg`, `deleteOrg`, `setCapabilities` and `setAllApps`; mero-js has a
builder for each (`releaseConsent`, `upgradeConsent`, `createOrgConsent`, ...).

- For a package-bound session, `returnTo` must be on one of the package's
  own origins (its `{label}.D` and other hosts, a registered or served
  origin) or one its newest signed manifest names (`links.frontend`,
  `frontendAliases`); for an unbound session, one of the cluster's
  `--origins`. It is `https` (or `http` on `localhost`), without credentials
  or a fragment, at most 2 KiB: else `400 RETURN_TO_NOT_ALLOWED`
  (`allowed_return_to` in `crates/node/src/consent_page.rs`).
- Show the person the answer's `code` before you send them; the node's page
  shows the same code.
- An account has one undecided request per node: a new one replaces the
  older, whose result then answers `404` (`CONSENT_REPLACED` in mero-js). A
  request lives 10 minutes; a page whose subject changed meanwhile is
  `409 CONSENT_STALE`.
- `resumeConsent` throws `CONSENT_NOT_STARTED`, `CONSENT_REQUEST_MISMATCH` or
  `CONSENT_NOT_DECIDED` for a return it cannot vouch for: do not act on those.

The full list of subjects and what the page shows is in
[The consent page](/protocol/consent-page/); mero-js's
[user approvals guide](https://calimero-network.github.io/mero-js/guides/user-approvals/)
covers the client side.

## Serve it on your own domain

Two kinds of origin can sign people in to a package besides its `{label}.D`
host, both registered by the package's manager (its publisher organization's
org-wide `MANAGE_APPLICATION` holders, else the account that installed it
first) with their passkey:

- A **registered origin** (`https://notes.example.com`): your own hosting
  serves the page, and passkey ceremonies there run under that domain's
  relying-party id. Sessions opened there are bound to the package and name
  the origin; removing the origin ends them.
- A **served origin** (`served: true`): the cluster also serves the package's
  frontend there from the signed bundle, the same site as `{label}.D`. It must
  be `https` with no port, not under the apps domain or the cluster's rp-id;
  browsers reach it once Calimero Cloud holds its certificate and route.

```bash
meroctl app origins add com.example.notes https://notes.example.com --served
meroctl app origins list com.example.notes
meroctl app origins remove com.example.notes https://notes.example.com
```

```ts
import { browserPasskey, passkeyConfirm } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';

// From a session on the cluster's own origin: a package-bound session cannot manage origins.
await client.packages.originsAdd(
  { package: 'com.example.notes', origin: 'https://notes.example.com', served: true },
  { confirm: passkeyConfirm(browserPasskey()) },
);
```

| Limit or refusal | When |
| --- | --- |
| 8 origins per package; 4 served per package, 64 per cluster | |
| `403 ORIGIN_NOT_REGISTERED` | a sign-in or sign-up from an origin the package has not registered |
| `400 NOT_SERVING` | `--served` on a cluster without `--apps-domain` |
| `409 ORIGIN_TAKEN` | the origin is held with the other `served`; remove it first |
| `409 CLUSTER_NOT_UPGRADED` | a served origin while a node runs an older release |
| `http` origins | only `localhost` names, on a `--dev` node |

<Aside type="tip">
  Removing an origin ends every session opened there: their next request is
  `401`. Move people to the new origin before you remove the old one, and list
  the old one in `frontendAliases` while links to it are still around.
</Aside>
